title: Causal Convolution
tagline: Slide a kernel over a sequence without ever peeking into the future — with left-padding and dilation as the two knobs that matter
summary: Drag a causal 1-D convolution across a sequence and watch the rules enforce themselves: the kernel at time t may only touch inputs at t and earlier, so the shaded future stays off-limits. Toggle left-padding to keep the output the same length as the input, and stretch the dilation to grow the receptive field (K-1)d+1 without adding a single weight. The building block behind WaveNet and Temporal Convolutional Networks, made tangible.
highlights: Watch causality as a masking rule: the kernel is physically blocked from crossing the 'now' line into the shaded future.
Toggle left-padding and see the output length snap from N-(K-1)d back to N, with padding zeros filling the missing past.
Stretch the dilation from 1 to 4 and watch the receptive field (K-1)d+1 grow while the weight count stays fixed at K.
Slide 'now' to the far left with padding off and see the oldest taps fall off the edge — no x[-1], no output.
Connects directly to WaveNet and TCNs, where dilations 1,2,4,8 give an exponentially growing receptive field.
